name: Rodrigo Paz Pereira
quote: "Se acabó el negocio de los delincuentes, subvención o futuro yo elijo futuro" — announced the total elimination of the diesel subsidy via Decree 5716 hours after Congress ratified the $1.9B IMF financing deal, Sept 19, 2026.

name: Edmand Lara
quote: "He visto a Fernando Cerimedo dando órdenes e instrucciones a los ministros" — said Sept 1, 2026 that forensic analysis of Cerimedo's devices showed "sustained contact" with the men accused of shooting Nadia Beller, publicly breaking with President Paz over the adviser's role. Convened the Legislative Assembly's Seventeenth Ordinary Session for Sep 16 at 16:00 to consider Decree 5707's 90-day state-of-exception extension, while himself questioning the need to prolong the measure. On Sept 1 he filed a criminal complaint against First Lady María Elena Urquidi and Cerimedo over the ouster of Police Commander Mirko Sokol, and on Sept 3 released a second disputed audio alleging Paz and Cerimedo scripted a "narrative" for the June 20 state-of-exception decree; some assembly members allege he acts on instructions from Evo Morales, which Lara denies.

name: José Luis Lupo
role: Former Minister of the Presidency (until Aug 3, 2026); nominated as ambassador to the OAS
quote: Coordinated the government's negotiating track with COB and sectoral protest groups throughout May and June, before being replaced by Fernando Aramayo on Aug 3, 2026.

name: Fernando Aramayo
role: Minister of the Presidency (since Aug 3, 2026; previously Foreign Minister)
quote: Told mayors and cabinet the diesel decree "is one of the conditions we have from the International Monetary Fund," rejecting calls to repeal it, Aug 27, 2026.

name: José Gabriel Espinoza
role: Former Minister of Economy and Public Finance (dismissed Aug 21, 2026)
quote: Censured by Congress (91-of-129 vote) for skipping a scheduled interpellation on bond issuances and budget delays; dismissed by presidential decree Aug 21, 2026.

name: Marco Antonio "Tuco" Oviedo
quote: "Existe un gran consenso ciudadano" for extending the state of exception 90 more days, Sept 13, 2026.

name: Ernesto Justiniano
quote: Confirmed the cabinet's Sep 14 approval of Decree 5707 extending the state of exception 90 more days: "Esperamos que el Congreso apruebe este decreto para que podamos ampliar" the emergency measures while risk factors persist. Previously oversaw the joint police-military operations to clear blockades, including the June 6 Route 9 action, and ordered a preventive troop deployment to Yapacaní on Aug 25.

name: Mario Argollo
quote: Convened an undated COB national emergency assembly (ampliado) over Decree 5716's diesel-subsidy elimination, saying the government is "the only responsible party for social instability" for breaking prior agreements, Sept 19-20, 2026. Previously rejected the state-of-exception extension Sept 16 as legally unjustified.

name: Evo Morales
role: Former President; cocalero federation and MAS leader
quote: "Oportunamente dijimos [Rodrigo Paz] es un presidente por accidente. Ahora se demuestra eso" — told supporters in Ivirgarzama Paz was an "accidental president," Aug 26, 2026.

name: Leonardo Loza
quote: Amplified calls for Paz's resignation alongside Evo Morales's 190km march into La Paz.

name: Vicente Salazar
quote: Arrested in early July 2026 amid the government's crackdown on blockade organizers.

name: Alberto Quelali
quote: Arrested June 26, 2026, after leading FEJUVE's declaration of a city-wide emergency in El Alto.

name: Eliser Roca
quote: Losing roughly US$6.5 million per day.

name: Sebastián Daroca
quote: Announced the two-tier diesel pricing decree (Bs. 18/L for large consumers) intended to close the smuggling margin and end fuel-station queues, Aug 17, 2026.

name: Donald Trump
quote: Characterized the protests as an attempted coup and blamed narco-terrorists for driving the unrest.

name: Javier Milei
quote: Sent two C-130 Hercules aircraft to Bolivia, described by his government as humanitarian aid.

name: Gustavo Petro
quote: Voiced support for the protesters, prompting Bolivia to expel Colombian ambassador Elizabeth García on May 20, 2026.

name: Fernando Cerimedo
role: Argentine political consultant; informal adviser to Paz's 2025 campaign
quote: Ordered into 180 days of preventive detention, initially at Palmasola prison, Aug 21, 2026, after prosecutors charged him with attempted femicide against former partner Nadia Beller; now held at the high-security Chonchocoro facility. Attorney General Roger Mariaca announced Sept 9 that prosecutors added usurpation-of-functions and money-laundering charges, bringing his concurrent cases to four alongside the Beni drug-trafficking-flights probe.

name: Nadia Beller
role: Lawyer; Fernando Cerimedo's former partner and shooting victim
quote: Called the Aug 17 shooting a "state crime" implicating government and police after phone messages surfaced linking a contact to the government's intelligence chief, and demanded President Paz break his public silence, Aug 22, 2026. Expanded her declaration to prosecutors Sept 9, alleging Cerimedo "coordinaba con fuerzas del orden" (coordinated with law enforcement) during his informal advisory role; was summoned Sept 12 alongside businessman Robin Jofré Azzarini as a witness in the illicit-enrichment case, with her testimony to be taken via advance-proof procedure in Santa Cruz for health reasons stemming from the shooting.

name: Óscar Mario Justiniano Pinto
role: Minister of Sustainable Production, Environment and Water (reverted after 4-day interim stint at Economy)
quote: Served as interim Economy Minister Aug 21-25, 2026, after predecessor José Gabriel Espinoza's censure, until permanent successor Christian Morales Burgos was sworn in Aug 25.

name: Erik Correa González
role: Intelligence chief, Government of Rodrigo Paz (alleged)
quote: Identified by Nadia Beller and Evo Morales — based on phone messages recovered from Fernando Cerimedo's device — as the contact saved as "ECG" who allegedly tracked the Aug 17 attack on Beller in real time; has not publicly responded.

name: Isidro Auca
quote: "Este gobierno quiere rifar nuestros recursos naturales, no escucha al pueblo" — led thousands of coca growers marching into Cochabamba in defiance of the state of emergency, Sept 4, 2026.

name: Adrián Javier Álvarez Arismendi
role: Interim Commander General of the Bolivian Police (since Aug 31, 2026)
quote: Sworn in at the Palacio Quemado to replace Mirko Sokol, who resigned amid a corruption audio-leak probe; previously headed Police technology/telematics and the El Alto police district.

name: Roger Mariaca
quote: Announced Sept 9, 2026 that prosecutors expanded the case against Fernando Cerimedo to include usurpation of public functions and money laundering, saying a prosecutorial commission would take his expanded statement "within other criminal facts attributed to the defendant."

name: José Luis Gálvez
quote: "Si se ve pertinente imponer otras medidas, lo vamos a hacer, la ley lo contempla" — said Sept 16, 2026 the government could declare a state of siege, including possible curfews, if new road blockades materialize while the state-of-exception extension awaits a legislative vote.

name: Christian Andrés Morales Burgos
role: Minister of Economy and Public Finance (sworn in Aug 25, 2026; previously Vice Minister of Treasury and Public Credit)
quote: "Daremos continuidad a las medidas que se han venido implementando" — pledged policy continuity on being sworn in, while saying Aug 26 that Supreme Decree 5676 needs adjustments "to minimize risks" from the producer mobilizations it triggered.

name: Josué Caricari
role: President, Federación Nacional de Cooperativas Mineras (FENCOMIN)
quote: Called the 90-day extension of the state of exception a "mordaza" (gag) and "persecución" on Sept 17, 2026, and announced FENCOMIN would hold its own national assembly (ampliado nacional) to define the mining cooperatives' response, without setting a date.

name: Víctor Tarqui
role: Secretary General, Confederación de Choferes de Bolivia
quote: Declared the transport drivers' confederation in a state of emergency over Decree 5716's diesel-price hike and set a national assembly for Mon, Sep 21, 2026 to decide on protest measures, without ruling out strikes or road blockades.

name: Lucio Gómez
role: Leader, Confederación Sindical de Choferes de Bolivia
quote: "El lunes no habrá transporte público en el país" — announced a 24-hour national transport stoppage for Mon, Sep 28, 2026 across urban, interprovincial and international routes in rejection of Decree 5716's diesel-price hike, following a national meeting in Santa Cruz, and warned measures would grow "more forceful until reaching an indefinite general strike" if the government does not respond.
